where: Section 1 formula box, worked example step 1, exam trap 4
problem: Powers of ten are printed as plain digits: "1/(1 × 109) s", "Tb = 1/B is the bit period in ps" and "multiply by 1012 for ps". As printed, 1 × 109 reads as one hundred nine, so the shown equalities look wrong to a student.
fix: Use superscript tags: Tb = 1/(1 × 10<sup>9</sup>) s = 1 ns; multiply by 10<sup>12</sup> to convert seconds to ps. In the formula box write Tb = 10<sup>12</sup>/B ps with B in bit/s, because 1/B is in seconds before conversion.

problem: "their standard deviations add as squares" is wrong wording: it is the squares of the standard deviations (the variances) that add; the standard deviations themselves add in quadrature.
fix: Independent broadening mechanisms have additive variances, so T<sub>sys</sub> = √(T<sub>tx</sub>² + T<sub>fiber</sub>² + T<sub>rx</sub>²). Adding the rise times directly would overestimate the total spread.

problem: The symbol Tr is defined as the 10–90% rise time and then never used; the budget formula uses Ttx, Tfiber and Trx instead, which can make a student hunt for a missing term.
fix: Either drop Tr or say: "A pulse's own 10–90% rise time is Tr; in the budget below the three contributors are called T<sub>tx</sub>, T<sub>fiber</sub> and T<sub>rx</sub>."
